metadata.canonical_boundary: Bloodtrail is canonical. OCSF 1.8.0 is export-only. OpenTelemetry 1.59.0 and Semantic Conventions 1.43.0 are transport-only. CloudEvents 1.0.2 is optional envelope-only.

standards.name: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 AU controls
standards.normative_scope: AU-2, AU-3, AU-5, AU-8, AU-9, AU-11, AU-12 event selection, content, timestamp, protection, retention, and generation guidance.
facts: Identifies audit event selection and content concerns.
Does not define Bloodtrail JSON envelope, actor model, tenant authority, or producer SDK behavior.
standards.recommendation: Use as evidence input only; do not treat it as a complete Bloodtrail requirement.
standards.design_decision: Use NIST AU control objectives as evidence for event selection, content, timestamp, protection, retention, and generation concerns; Bloodtrail defines the project-specific contract.

standards.name: OCSF schema
standards.normative_scope: Cybersecurity event normalization categories, classes, profiles, objects, attributes, extensions, and versioning.
facts: Does not own Bloodtrail tenant, transaction, delivery, privacy, or producer authority semantics.
standards.recommendation: Use only at ingestion/export with tested event and field mappings.
standards.design_decision: Keep OCSF 1.8.0 as a version-pinned downstream ingestion/export mapping with explicit exact, transformed, extended, unmapped, and lossy status.

standards.name: OpenTelemetry Specification Logs Data Model
standards.normative_scope: LogRecord timestamps, trace/span context, resource, instrumentation scope, attributes, body, and event name fields.
facts: Supports native occurrence and observation time plus W3C trace/span fields.
Does not define Bloodtrail audit authority, privacy, catalog, or delivery classes.
standards.recommendation: Use only as optional transport representation.
standards.design_decision: Represent canonical occurrence/observation timestamps, trace/span context, resource, instrumentation scope, attributes, body, and event name through an optional OpenTelemetry transport mapping.

standards.name: OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions events guidance
standards.normative_scope: Stable event names without dynamic values and occurrence time guidance.
facts: Supports low-cardinality event naming and occurrence time separation.
Leaves domain event structure to Bloodtrail.
standards.design_decision: Use stable low-cardinality EventName and occurrence-time guidance in the optional OpenTelemetry transport mapping.

standards.name: CloudEvents specification
standards.normative_scope: Protocol-neutral event envelope context attributes and duplicate identity using source plus id.
facts: Defines envelope metadata and data separation.
Does not define canonical audit payload semantics or trust elevation.
standards.recommendation: Permit only optional envelope wrapping; reject envelope/payload conflicts.
standards.design_decision: Allow CloudEvents 1.0.2 only as an optional transport envelope; preserve the canonical event in data and reject envelope/payload conflicts.

standards.name: W3C Trace Context
standards.normative_scope: traceparent/tracestate trace-id and parent-id propagation plus privacy and trust-boundary considerations.
facts: Defines trace-id and span-id shape and propagation concerns.
Trace context is correlation-only, not identity or authorization.
standards.recommendation: Validate structure and restart/omit at trust boundaries when needed.
standards.design_decision: When trace context is present, validate W3C trace/span formats and treat propagated context as correlation-only and untrusted at external boundaries.

standards.name: JSON Schema
standards.normative_scope: Schema dialect, identifiers, references, vocabularies, validation, and unevaluated property behavior.
facts: Cannot express every producer authority or tenant/resource invariant alone.
standards.recommendation: Use Draft 2020-12 plus deterministic semantic validation.
standards.design_decision: Declare JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 for structural validation and supplement it with deterministic semantic validation for cross-field authority rules.

standards.name: Semantic Versioning
standards.normative_scope: Major, minor, and patch compatibility terminology after defining the public API.
facts: Provides vocabulary for compatible and incompatible change classes.
Bloodtrail must define its own compatibility surface first.
standards.recommendation: Apply to schema/catalog field paths, requiredness, privacy, authority, vocabularies, mappings, and validation results.
standards.design_decision: Apply SemVer terminology only after defining Bloodtrail public compatibility as field paths, types, authority, privacy, requiredness, catalog semantics, validation results, and mapping guarantees.

standards.name: OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet
standards.normative_scope: Application event logging selection, when/where/who/what context, sanitization, and data to exclude.
facts: Supports event selection, sanitization, and excluded-data reasoning.
Does not approve Bloodtrail retention, legal basis, or production architecture.
standards.recommendation: Use as privacy and misuse-resistance evidence input only.
standards.design_decision: Use allowlist-first event selection, sanitization, and excluded-data guidance to support Bloodtrail privacy and misuse-resistance policy without asserting external approval.

best_effort.semantic: At-most-once acceptable with bounded loss reporting.
best_effort.durability: direct attempt or bounded memory buffer
best_effort.idempotency: unique event id; duplicates tolerated but not guaranteed
best_effort.backpressure: drop with bounded counter and health signal

security_significant.semantic: At-least-once after required producer boundary accepts the occurrence.
security_significant.durability: durable or protected bounded queue in later implementation
security_significant.idempotency: same event id on retry; consumers dedupe
security_significant.retry: bounded retry with jitter and retry exhaustion alert
security_significant.business_failure_posture: normally fail_open unless event-specific policy strengthens

transaction_critical.semantic: Audit durability atomic with successful business commit; downstream at-least-once.
transaction_critical.durability: transactional outbox or equivalent behavior, product not selected
transaction_critical.idempotency: dedupe by event id and transaction id
transaction_critical.backpressure: commit gate before durability point; backlog alert after commit
transaction_critical.outage: defer downstream delivery from durable record
transaction_critical.business_failure_posture: fail_closed before business commit if audit durability cannot be reached

policy_critical.semantic: Policy owner must approve exact fail-open, fail-closed, or deferred-completion behavior before production.
policy_critical.durability: at least security-significant; may require transaction-critical semantics
policy_critical.idempotency: same event id on retry with policy-specific reconciliation
policy_critical.outage: production blocked until reviewed policy exists

adrs.title: Bloodtrail-owned canonical model versus direct OCSF
adrs.decision: Bloodtrail owns the canonical application-facing model; OCSF 1.8.0 is export-only at ingestion/export.
consequences: Producers do not emit OCSF numeric classes as authoritative fields.
Mapping losses are explicit and tested.
unresolved: Final approval commit pending project owner review.

adrs.title: Authoritative source and JSON Schema dialect
adrs.decision: contracts/security-audit/source/contract.source.json is the sole authored source. Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema is generated with deterministic provenance.
consequences: Human docs, schema, examples, mappings, and tests are generated or cross-checked from one source.
No TypeScript source becomes schema authority.
unresolved: Generated TypeScript may be added only in a later SDK change.

adrs.title: Identifier timestamp and causality formats
adrs.decision: Opaque UUID event IDs, RFC 3339 UTC timestamps, zero-based retry attempts, 300 second skew alert threshold, and W3C trace/span as correlation-only context.
consequences: Event ID remains stable on redelivery.
Trace IDs are never identity or authorization evidence.
unresolved: Concrete clock and ID library selection is deferred to later implementation.

adrs.title: OpenTelemetry and CloudEvents representation
adrs.decision: OpenTelemetry 1.59.0/SemConv 1.43.0 are transport-only; native timestamps, trace/span, resource, instrumentation scope, and EventName are used. CloudEvents 1.0.2 remains optional envelope-only.
unresolved: No collector, exporter, or protocol binding is selected here.

adrs.title: Delivery classes and failure posture
adrs.decision: best_effort, security_significant, transaction_critical, and policy_critical classes define observable behavior without selecting queue, broker, collector, or outbox products.
consequences: Catalog assigns exactly one minimum class per event.
Policy-critical production remains blocked without qualified review.
unresolved: Actual alert thresholds and policy-critical posture require future owner approval.

adrs.title: Privacy pseudonymization and retention classes
adrs.decision: Every field has allowed, conditionally_allowed, transform_required, or prohibited policy. Purpose- and tenant-scoped keyed transforms are the default for direct identifiers when direct display is unnecessary.
consequences: Secrets and raw bodies are prohibited everywhere, including examples and diagnostics.
Actual retention durations and legal basis are not invented.
unresolved: Durations, residency, legal hold, and cross-tenant export require qualified review.

adrs.title: Actor tenant and resource authority
adrs.decision: Actor, subject, authenticated principal, delegation/impersonation, credential, service/workload, tenant hierarchy, and resource-owner fields have separate authority and trust rules.
consequences: Client claimed tenant or browser data cannot become authoritative by relabeling.
Cross-tenant and platform actions require explicit policy context.
unresolved: Concrete tenancy and identity providers are later implementation choices.

adrs.title: Schema evolution and compatibility
adrs.decision: SemVer applies to field paths, types, authority, privacy, requiredness, catalog meanings, validation results, and mapping guarantees. Required or semantic changes are major.
consequences: Compatibility fixtures define expected producer and consumer behavior.
unresolved: Removal windows need project-owner policy before release.
